title: Ell-p smooth convex optimization with a common minimizer localized in two norms
summary: A globally ell-p smooth convex objective has one minimizer satisfying simultaneous Euclidean and ell-p radius bounds. Queries and outputs are unrestricted in the full space.

description_paragraphs: Minimize an unknown convex objective globally on $\mathbb R^d$ using exact function values and full gradients.
task.formulation: Minimize an unknown convex objective globally on $\mathbb R^d$ using exact function values and full gradients.

description_paragraphs: For $2\le p\le\infty$, $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is convex and differentiable, and $$\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_{p^*}\le L\|x-y\|_p\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^d),$$ where $1/p+1/p^*=1$.

There exists one attained global minimizer $x^\star$ satisfying both $\|x^\star\|_2\le R_2$ and $\|x^\star\|_p\le R_p$. The two bounds concern the same minimizer. They impose no restriction on queries or outputs.

description_paragraphs: At any finite $x\in\mathbb R^d$, one query returns $(f(x),\nabla f(x))$ exactly. The public inputs are $d,p,L,R_2,R_p,\varepsilon$ and, for the probability criterion, $\delta$. The function and a minimizer are hidden.

description_paragraphs: Return any measurable point $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ determined by the transcript, possibly unqueried. No value or optimality certificate is required.
output.feasibility: Return any measurable point $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ determined by the transcript, possibly unqueried. No value or optimality certificate is required.

description_paragraphs: The base loss is $f(\widehat x)-f^\star$, where $f^\star=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}f(x)$.
metric.base_expression: The base loss is $f(\widehat x)-f^\star$, where $f^\star=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}f(x)$.

description_paragraphs: The algorithm is deterministic and adaptive. Queries, stopping, and the output may use the complete preceding transcript. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged. The stated budget holds on every admissible instance and every response history.

relations.description: The existing two-radius profile assumes Euclidean gradient smoothness. This profile imposes ell-p-to-dual-ell-p smoothness and retains the two independent radii of one common minimizer.
